title: Lesson 38 - Running User Permissions, Action Execution Context, and the Trust Layer Boundary
description: Explain the security context in which the agent is actually running, and how it impacts agent action execution.

questions.question: An action passes in the builder but fails for a customer in production. What is the most useful first step?
options: Add more actions to the topic
Check the running user's permissions and the action's run context, since the builder ran under your identity and production runs under the agent user
questions.explanation: The builder runs under the admin identity while production runs as the agent user or the employee, so the recovery starts by checking the running user's access and the action's execution context.

questions.question: A Flow action reaches records the running user should not be able to see. What most likely explains it?
options: The Flow runs in system context or the Apex runs without sharing, so it can reach beyond the running user's access
The agent has too many topics
questions.explanation: A Flow in system context or Apex without sharing can exceed the running user's reach, which is exactly why the action's execution context must be reviewed alongside the running user.

questions.question: Which statement about the Einstein Trust Layer for agents is correct?
options: It enforces record-level sharing for the agent
It replaces the need for least privilege on the agent user
Its data masking is applied to every agent response by default
It governs model traffic with injection filtering, toxicity checks, and audit logging, and record access stays with the running user
questions.explanation: The Trust Layer operates at inference time on model traffic, and because its data masking is not applied for agents, record-level access remains the running user's responsibility.
